title: Spin-Hall devices: spin relaxation spatially separates current injection from Joule dissipation
authors: Yanbo Qiao, Sariah Al Saati, Jean-Eric Wegrowe
abstract: The stationary state of a spin Hall bar connected to an external load circuit is investigated through a variational approach based on the principle of minimum power dissipation generalized to the two-spin-channel model. The self-consistent distributions of longitudinal and transverse current densities, alongside the corresponding spin and charge accumulations and dissipation power in the resistance, are derived. Surprisingly, it is shown that the Joule dissipation vanishes when the load resistance is placed at a sufficiently large distance compared with the spin-relaxation length. Such a highly non-trivial global stationary state appears as the most striking characteristic of the injection of pure spin current compared with more usual current injection.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes current flow in a spin-Hall device using variational methods based on minimum power dissipation. The key finding is that strong spin relaxation fundamentally alters the system's stationary state, causing the Joule heating in an external load to vanish under certain conditions. This demonstrates a spatial decoupling between pure spin current injection and energy dissipation.
main_problem: The study investigates how spin relaxation spatially separates current injection from Joule dissipation when analyzing the stationary state of a spin-Hall bar connected to an external load circuit.
main_result: It is shown that under conditions of strong spin relaxation, the Joule dissipation in the load resistance vanishes, indicating a non-trivial separation between injected pure spin current and energy dissipation.
method: The analysis employs a variational approach based on minimizing power dissipation (or entropy production) within a two-spin-channel model framework.
model_or_system: The system is a homogeneous, non-magnetic conducting layer (spin-Hall bar) modeled with two spin channels ($\uparrow$ and $\downarrow$), driven by an external electric field and connected to a load resistance $R_\ell$.
key_observables: Longitudinal and transverse current densities ($J_{x\sigma}, J_{y\sigma}$), charge/spin accumulations, and the total Joule dissipation power in the load.
important_parameters: The dimensionless control parameter $\alpha = R/R_\ell$ (load resistance vs. internal resistance) and the spin-relaxation length ($\lambda_{sf}$) relative to the device dimensions ($\ell$).
main_assumptions: Assumptions include longitudinal invariance ($\partial_x=0$), small Hall angle ($	heta \ll 1$), and linear response for spin-flip processes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate normalized spatial profiles of transverse spin current, spin accumulation, and the load power ratio ($P_{	ext{load}}/P_0$) as a function of $\alpha$ and $\lambda_{sf}/\ell$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by setting up the variational principle for the stationary state, deriving coupled differential equations for current profiles, analyzing limiting cases (e.g., open/short circuit), and finally quantifying the load power dependence on spin relaxation strength.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the use of minimum dissipation principles and non-equilibrium thermodynamics connects to general frameworks used in studying energy flow and steady states in complex quantum systems.
